title: The Most Important Choe Show Interview
summary: A 30-second official-channel opening to a two-person Choe Show interview. One participant calls it the most important interview in a larger project while acknowledging the pressure that creates, then admits not understanding why they are doing something. The other challenges that uncertainty. They invoke a strange shared life and having been together “through everything” before the interviewer asks whether the person has been described as angry. The response—“don’t do this, don’t start it off like this”—is explicit resistance and remains central. The excerpt closes with an impression that the person does not discuss emotions much, before any answer. Importance, anger and emotional disclosure are claims/questions rather than diagnoses. The title and adjacency do not publisher-label either voice; zero named turns ship.
